incidents.vector: Russia-based operators ran a botnet using Solana blockchain, BitTorrent, Google Calendar and rented VPS infrastructure to push malware into VS Code extensions, npm and Python packages and more than 300 GitHub repositories since early 2025.
incidents.impact: CrowdStrike, Google, and Shadowserver simultaneously seized four attacker servers, disrupting the botnet's command channels and the GlasswormRAT remote-access tool that had stolen data and credentials from Windows, macOS and Linux developer machines worldwide.

incidents.victim: Kimwolf DDoS botnet (millions of IoT devices)
incidents.vector: A 23-year-old Ottawa resident allegedly built and rented out an IoT botnet that enslaved millions of cameras, photo frames and similar devices, generating record DDoS attacks measured near 30 Tbps including hits against US Department of Defense IP ranges.
incidents.impact: Canadian police arrested the suspect on a US extradition warrant; some victims incurred losses exceeding $1 million and the botnet issued over 25,000 attack commands before international takedowns of Kimwolf, Aisuru, JackSkid and Mossad infrastructure.

incidents.vector: An unpatched vulnerability in Ajax's ticketing systems allowed an intruder to repeatedly access club computers, exposing supporter email addresses, season-ticket records and stadium-ban data; the attacker could also transfer tickets and alter ban records.
incidents.impact: Dutch national police arrested a 35-year-old man in Buren on May 27 in connection with the March breach, which reporting suggests may have exposed personal data on more than 300,000 registered supporters and 42,000 season tickets.

incidents.victim: Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (LACMTA)
incidents.vector: MOIS-linked operators posing as a hacktivist group exfiltrated data, then combined scripted destruction with hands-on-keyboard activity to wipe databases, virtual machines and storage volumes across virtualization, backup and storage layers to deny recovery.
incidents.impact: Israeli firm Gambit Security tied the March breach of LA's transit authority to Iran's MOIS, confirming at least 700 GB of emails, backups and files were stolen and parts of the transit network were forced offline.

incidents.victim: South Florida Tri-Rail, Vyncs vehicle tracking, Saudi infrastructure firm Unimac, plus Israeli media and academic targets
incidents.vector: The same Iran-state-directed cluster behind the LACMTA breach used custom exfiltration tooling and destructive scripting to compromise additional transit, vehicle-tracking and infrastructure firms, exposing data online in some cases.
incidents.impact: Tri-Rail confirmed a hack but said no critical data was affected; Vyncs detected its intrusion on April 2 and the FBI is involved; Israeli organizations and a Turkish insurance brokerage were also breached by the same group.

incidents.vector: A phishing email led to compromise of Microsoft 365 mailboxes belonging to firm personnel, with attackers maintaining persistent access for roughly 11 months before detection; the firm allegedly lacked MFA and basic safeguards.
incidents.impact: A proposed class action filed this week alleges hackers tied to the Chinese government accessed Wiley Rein M365 accounts from July 2024 to June 2025, stealing names, SSNs, financial accounts, medical and other PII; victims report fraudulent charges since the breach.

incidents.vector: A six-hour automated campaign dubbed Megalodon used dummy GitHub accounts and forged author identities to push 5,718 commits injecting malicious GitHub Actions workflows that exfiltrate CI/CD secrets, cloud credentials, SSH keys and OIDC tokens.
incidents.impact: More than 5,500 repositories were poisoned starting May 18; about 2,900 remained infected a week later, and downstream consumers of compromised packages such as Tiledesk inadvertently spread infections further.

incidents.vector: Operators ran SEO poisoning against utilities like CrystalDiskInfo and HWMonitor and even surfaced malicious download links inside AI chatbot answers; victims downloaded a ZIP that DLL-sideloaded malware, silently installed ScreenConnect remote-management, then deployed a process-hollowing GPU miner with six persistence mechanisms.
incidents.impact: Microsoft identified more than 150 malicious lookalike domains since March; compromised systems gain persistent attacker access via ScreenConnect that could later support data theft, lateral movement or ransomware in addition to GPU mining.

incidents.victim: US law firms (and healthcare, insurance, financial sectors)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — data extortion (Silent Ransom Group / Luna Moth, ex-Conti)
incidents.vector: Operators combine phishing emails, callback-style fake IT-support phone calls and even in-person visits to firm offices, persuading staff to grant remote desktop access or attaching USB devices under the pretext of a security backup.
incidents.impact: The FBI advisory issued Tuesday warns that Silent Ransom Group (also tracked as Luna Moth, Chatty Spider, UNC3753) is using legitimate remote-management tools and Google Drive/OneDrive to exfiltrate sensitive legal data for extortion, with US law firms continuously targeted since 2023.

incidents.attacker: Unknown — insider exposure (no malicious actor confirmed)
incidents.vector: A CISA contractor created a public GitHub profile called "Private-CISA" and intentionally disabled GitHub's built-in secrets protection, publishing 844 MB of plaintext passwords, AWS GovCloud keys, authentication tokens and an RSA key granting full access to all CISA-IT repositories.
incidents.impact: More than a week after notification, CISA was still working to invalidate exposed credentials; experts warned an attacker holding the leaked key could read every CISA-IT private repo, hijack CI/CD pipelines and modify branch protections. Congressional leaders are demanding answers about CISA's internal controls.

incidents.victim: Japanese KnowledgeDeliver (Digital Knowledge) Learning Management System customers
incidents.vector: Threat actors exploited hardcoded ASP.NET machineKey values shipped in KnowledgeDeliver's default web.config (CVE-2026-5426), forging ViewState payloads for unauthenticated remote code execution, then deployed the in-memory BLUEBEAM/Godzilla web shell, tampered with site JavaScript and distributed a Cobalt Strike BEACON installer customized for the target.
incidents.impact: Mandiant disclosed the zero-day campaign that compromised a Japanese LMS server in late 2025; because the same hardcoded keys existed across many customer deployments before Feb 24, 2026, every internet-facing KnowledgeDeliver instance was potentially exposed.

incidents.victim: Aerospace, defense and telecom firms in the US, Israel, UAE and other Middle Eastern entities
incidents.vector: The Iran-nexus APT (UNC1549) sent personalized recruitment-themed spear-phishing lures impersonating airline and video-conferencing brands, used DLL sideloading for execution, and abused AppDomainManager hijacking to disable .NET application security so newly developed RATs (MiniUpdate and MiniJunk V2) could operate.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 identified six new RAT variants deployed between February and April 2026 against entities in the US, Israel and UAE; timing aligned with the regional conflict that began Feb 28, 2026, and the group routed C2 through unique Azure-hosted domains per target.

incidents.vector: Attackers gained access to systems holding patient records and biometric data; specific intrusion technique was not disclosed.
incidents.impact: At least 1.8 million people had medical data, fingerprints and palm prints stolen — biometric identifiers that cannot be replaced, raising long-term identity-theft and re-identification risk for the affected patients.

incidents.vector: A GitHub employee downloaded a poisoned VS Code extension that stole the user's credentials and access; the TeamPCP gang then exfiltrated source code from approximately 4,000 internal repositories.
incidents.impact: TeamPCP claimed responsibility for the theft of roughly 4,000 GitHub internal private repositories. The breach underscores the gang's pivot from npm worm campaigns to compromising developer tooling at trusted vendors.

incidents.vector: Fox Tempest operated fake Microsoft accounts and abused Microsoft's Artifact Signing service to sign customer-supplied malware so it appeared legitimate; downstream actors then distributed the signed payloads via search manipulation and malvertising.
incidents.impact: Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit obtained a court order in SDNY, seized signspace[.]cloud, took hundreds of operator VMs offline and revoked fraudulently obtained certificates. The action also named Vanilla Tempest as a co-conspirator that used the service to deploy Rhysida ransomware, Oyster, Lumma Stealer and Vidar, and disclosed links to INC, Qilin and Akira affiliates.

incidents.vector: Dutch investigators acted on evidence that WorkTitans and MIRhosting were the most-used networks in pro-Russian DDoS and influence attacks on Danish government targets during the November 2025 municipal elections, and that the network had absorbed sanctioned Stark Industries infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Dutch FIOD agents arrested two co-owners (a 57-year-old in Amsterdam and a 39-year-old Russian-born operator in The Hague), searched five sites and seized more than 800 servers along with laptops and phones. Customer data on the seized servers was permanently lost.

incidents.victim: Dozens of enterprises in North America, Australia and the UK (Microsoft 365 / Okta tenants)
incidents.vector: Operators ran high-volume voice phishing to personal cell phones impersonating IT help-desk staff about a passkey or MFA migration, then ran a live adversary-in-the-middle on lookalike SSO portals to capture credentials and MFA codes and registered attacker-controlled MFA devices for persistence.
incidents.impact: Mandiant assesses dozens of organizations have been compromised since early 2026; once inside, BlackFile used Python scripts and Microsoft Graph API to programmatically exfiltrate hundreds of thousands to millions of files from SharePoint, OneDrive, Salesforce and Zendesk, with ransom demands starting in the millions and escalating with swatting and executive harassment when ignored.

incidents.vector: MOIS-linked operators using the Handala hacktivist persona breached the manufacturer and executed wiping operations against employee endpoints and internal systems.
incidents.impact: The March attack crippled the company by wiping employee devices and corporate systems. Researchers and the DOJ link Handala to Iranian intelligence despite its public hacktivist branding.

incidents.vector: A cluster of 126 Chrome extensions advertised as WhatsApp business helpers (WaSteal) intercepted WhatsApp web content, including messages, session cookies and audio, exfiltrating it to attacker infrastructure.
incidents.impact: More than 146,000 installations primarily in Brazil were affected, exposing message content, account credentials and audio data; victims face account takeover and fraud risk.

incidents.victim: Transit Finance and TAC cross-chain DeFi platforms
incidents.vector: Hackers exploited a four-year-old legacy smart contract on Transit Finance and a similar vulnerable contract interacting with the TON blockchain on TAC.
incidents.impact: Approximately $1.9 million was drained from Transit Finance and $2.8 million from TAC on the same day. Transit Finance pledged to compensate affected users.

incidents.victim: TanStack, OpenSearch, Mistral AI, UiPath, Intercom, OpenAI and 160+ other npm publishers
incidents.vector: Attackers chained three GitHub Actions weaknesses — pwn-request, cache poisoning and OIDC token extraction from runner memory — to publish 84 malicious package artifacts across 42 @tanstack/* packages without any stolen credential. Self-propagation then spread the worm via stolen tokens.
incidents.impact: By end of day, 373 malicious npm versions across 169 packages plus PyPI packages were published, including OpenSearch's official JS client, 57 UiPath packages, the Mistral AI TypeScript SDK and Intercom; affected packages had roughly 520 million cumulative downloads in the exposure window. OpenAI confirmed two employee devices were impacted and rotated code-signing certificates. This is also the first documented worm to publish npm packages with valid SLSA Build Level 3 provenance.
